checklist.item: Secrets and server texts (tokens, header values, SMTP or upstream replies, file contents) in errors, logs and responses.
checklist.evidence: Running service in token mode, debug log level; the fake api serves 6 database channels with hostile references (a secret that is not a URL, a symlink out of the secret directory, a non-prefixed env name, an http Slack URL, a webhook URL with user info and query, an SMTP password file). 7 markers (4 secret values, the content of the file behind the symlink, the secret file content, the service token): 0 times in the service log, 0 times in the PUT /service/notify/report bodies. Report rejections hold fixed texts with reference names only: 'channel "b": urlEnv does not hold a valid url', 'channel "c": urlFile: outside-link is outside the secret directory', 'channel "f": urlEnv must hold an https url', 'channels[3].urlEnv: must match ^PULSE_NOTIFY_SECRET_[A-Z0-9_]{1,64}$'. Failed webhook: 'webhook request failed' + ConnectionRefused, no URL. SMTP stub answers AUTH 535 and 454 with a marker text: 'SMTP AUTH failed: 535' (permanent, EAUTH) and 'SMTP AUTH failed: 454'; marker in log 0, in report 0, password in log 0. Service token, 6 bad setups (space, non-ASCII, both variables, empty, missing, unreadable file): exit 2 each with a fixed line, never the token. Upstream failures: 'GET service/notify/channels returned 307', 'claim failed: http', 'service report failed' (reason http), 'GET incidents returned 302'. Repository tests 'server text and token are absent across service failures' and 'every feed drops response markers across failure categories' pass. Findings: security-notify-2026-11-07-1, security-notify-2026-11-07-2.

checklist.item: Authentication before any other check; status codes and their order on admin routes.
checklist.evidence: notify has no admin or authenticated routes; its only listener is the pulse-kit ops listener, unauthenticated by design. Observed with curl -X <method> on the running service: /nope and /admin give 404 for GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS, PATCH, TRACE; /healthz, /readyz, /metrics give 405 for every method except GET and HEAD, then 200 or 503 ('polls failing (88 in a row)'). As a client, notify sends its token only on /service/*: the fake api saw 36 public reads with no authorization header and 36 /service/* calls with 'Bearer <36 chars>'.

checklist.item: Body and size limits on every method, also before any write.
checklist.evidence: Ops listener: POST /healthz with 100 MB gives 405 with 0 bytes uploaded; GET /metrics with a 100 MB body and GET /healthz with a 100 MB chunked body give 200; GET /metrics with a 500 MB chunked body gives 200 with service RSS 64,576 kB before and 66,112 kB after (drained, not buffered); a 64 KB header gives 431; no ops request writes. Outbound: /service/* answers capped at 1,048,576 bytes, feeds at PULSE_NOTIFY_API_MAX_BYTES, also chunked or gzip (tests 'service reads refuse oversized, wrong-wire, malformed and redirected answers', 'GET POST PUT bound decoded chunked and gzip answers', 'compressed and chunked oversized bodies fail on all feeds', test/api-limits.test.ts: pass). Channel rows are written only after the envelope and element checks (src/channel-sync.ts:256-296). The report is cut to 524,288 bytes (src/service-report.ts trimToSize). Local files (config, token file, secret files, state) are read whole without a cap; they are operator files.

checklist.item: Input validation at every trust boundary; validators never throw on any input type.
checklist.evidence: Extra test in the copy: 12 hostile inputs (getter object, Proxy with throwing traps, envelope with a getter or Proxy element, Symbol, BigInt, function, 100,000-deep array, __proto__ key from JSON.parse, null, string, NaN) x 4 validators (checkChannelsAnswer, validateServiceNotifyChannels, validateNotifyChannelRecord, validateResendClaimResponse): 'inputs=48 threw=0 accepted=0', Object.prototype unchanged. Hostile feed items on the running service (incident with a 200 KB object id, incident with a 100,000-character unknown key, manual incident with an object id): 'incident skipped: malformed data' reason 'invalid', longest log line 147 bytes, the valid incident 9 delivered, /readyz 200 ok. Reserved ids __proto__, constructor, toString, hasOwnProperty in the channel file: accepted, SQLite ledger seeds them, Object.prototype unchanged. Database ids must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$ and type file is refused by the contract. A database email channel with U+0085, U+2028, U+000B and a 'Bcc:' text in from, to and subjectPrefix: delivered, 0 header lines start with Bcc. Finding: security-notify-2026-11-07-3.

checklist.item: No accessor or getter of untrusted input runs.
checklist.evidence: All untrusted data enters as text through JSON.parse (feeds and /service/* answers through contract fetchJson and requestJson, the channel file, stored channel definitions and payloads), which creates data properties only. Probe: getter objects ran 0 getters in all 4 validators; a Proxy (cannot come from JSON.parse) got 1 trap call per validator call and no call threw. notify reads raw ids with Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor (src/api.ts:59, :217).

checklist.item: SSRF: allowed targets, environment lookups, redirects (cross-origin, https to http), forwarded headers.
checklist.evidence: Allowed targets: file channels come from the operator config; database channels take webhook, Slack and Teams URLs only from references (urlEnv, urlFile), never a literal, so the api cannot pick a URL; Slack and Teams need https (http only on loopback). Exception: the api picks the SMTP host and port of a database email channel (contract src/notify-channels.ts:152), see security-notify-2026-11-07-1 and note N2. Environment lookups: a database channel sees only PULSE_NOTIFY_SECRET_* (src/remote-channels.ts:142-148); a reference to PULSE_NOTIFY_API_TOKEN is refused. Bun fetch uses HTTP_PROXY from the environment (note N1). Redirects: running service against a fake api that answers 307 on /service/* and 302 on the public feeds with a location on another origin: GET, POST, PUT fail ('returned 307', 'claim failed: http', 'service report failed'), feeds fail with 'GET incidents returned 302', 0 requests at the redirect target. Webhook POST sets redirect 'manual' (src/channels/http-post.ts:44). Tests 'GET POST PUT refuse redirects without forwarding Bearer', 'no redirect is followed, cross-origin or same-origin', 'injected 5000ms timeout aborts GET POST PUT and forbids HTTPS downgrade' pass. Forwarded headers: the ops listener reads only method and path; an absolute-form request target gets 404.

Ledger: SQLite, WAL, synchronous FULL, one transaction per change. 15 kill -9 runs during deliveries (two file channels, 50 ms polls): PRAGMA integrity_check ok in 15 of 15; each restart took over the stale lock and resent pending keys; final state 1002 delivered, 1 pending, 48 seeded. Modes: state, -wal, -shm 0600, lock 0644. Temporary files: pulse-kit writeFileAtomicSync opens a random-suffix temp with wx (kit src/atomic-write.ts:133, :231); the migration creates <state>.migrating with wx (src/ledger.ts:712); lock and takeover marker with wx (src/ledger-lock.ts:169, :231); test 'migration and manual seed must not follow a planted .migrating symlink' passes. Paths come only from env and the operator config; a database channel cannot be type file; a secret file reference is a basename resolved with realpath inside PULSE_NOTIFY_SECRET_DIR (a symlink out is refused). The file channel appends one JSON line per notification.

checklist.evidence: package.json exact: runtime nodemailer 10.3.1, zod 4.6.7, contract and kit by full SHA; dev @biomejs/biome 2.6.3, lefthook 2.2.2, @types/node 26.6.6, @types/nodemailer 8.0.2, @types/bun 1.4.0, typescript7 npm:typescript@7.0.2, pulse-config by SHA. All approved (pulse-config not listed, note N5). Pins are ancestors of main (gh compare: behind_by=0). bun audit exit 1: minimatch@10.2.6 moderate GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249, dev only via eslint of pulse-config (note N3). Docker: both stages oven/bun:1.4.0-alpine@sha256:07235578...437eb, the approved digest; docker buildx imagetools inspect shows the same digest. Built image: uid=1000(bun), /app holds node_modules (contract, kit, nodemailer, zod), package.json, src; no git, 0 test files. CI: ci.yml actions/checkout@3d3c42e (v7.0.1, approved for targets) with persist-credentials: false; pulse-config 04108fa check.yml and release.yml: checkout v7.0.1 x5 with persist-credentials: false x5, oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e (v2.2.0), actions/attest@1e69f48 (v4.2.2), all approved. bun run lint (with the pulse-workflows action policy) passes.

findings.title: Database channels can send any notify secret to an SMTP host that the api chooses
findings.class: secret exfiltration (confused deputy): a secret reference is not bound to a destination
findings.command: Fake api serves one database email channel whose SMTP host is a stub chosen by the api and whose password reference names a secret the operator set for another purpose (a PULSE_NOTIFY_SECRET_* variable; a file in PULSE_NOTIFY_SECRET_DIR; implicit TLS to a non-loopback address with a CA trusted by notify). Run the service in token mode until one incident is delivered; expectation check: the stub must not receive a notify secret at AUTH.
findings.excerpt: stub: AUTH PLAIN user=<user chosen by the api> password=<value of the operator's PULSE_NOTIFY_SECRET_SLACK_URL>; second run: password=<content of a file in PULSE_NOTIFY_SECRET_DIR>; third run over TLS to 127.0.0.2: password=<value of PULSE_NOTIFY_SECRET_TEAMS_URL>. notify log: "msg":"notification delivered","channel":"mail", no warning. Expectation check exit 1 in 3 of 3 runs.
findings.impact: Whoever holds an api token with the admin scope (the console Owner role, automation or stolen tokens) can read the value of every PULSE_NOTIFY_SECRET_* variable and every top-level file in PULSE_NOTIFY_SECRET_DIR (Slack and Teams webhook URLs, webhook signing secrets, SMTP passwords), which the api and console otherwise never see (docs/channels.md:203, api docs/rest-api.md:557). The probe closes the same class with PULSE_PROBE_HEADER_HOSTS (api docs/operation.md:207); notify has no such binding and does not document the authority.
findings.fixDirection: Let the operator bind each secret reference to the destinations it may go to, as the probe does: for example a notify setting that maps each PULSE_NOTIFY_SECRET_* name and secret file to its allowed SMTP hosts (and URL hosts), or an operator allow-list of SMTP hosts for database channels; refuse a channel that breaks the binding with a fixed reason. Until then, document that an admin token is as sensitive as every secret notify can resolve.

findings.title: Config and state parse errors repeat a word of the file, now also in the live reload log
findings.command: Config file that is not JSON with a bare word at the first invalid position: start the service; replace a valid file with such a file while the service runs; a state file of the same kind with 'failed list'.
findings.excerpt: pulse-notify: config file <dir>/bad.json is not valid JSON: JSON Parse error: Unexpected identifier "FILETOKEN_7731" (exit 2); reload: {"level":"warn","msg":"channel file is invalid, keeping the last good channels","error":"config file <path> is not valid JSON","cause":"JSON Parse error: Unexpected identifier \"RELOADTOKEN_9953\""}; pulse-notify: cannot use state file <path>: JSON Parse error: Unexpected identifier "STATETOKEN_8842" (exit 2). Also src/index.ts:441 with errorFields (cause logged) and src/index.ts:151.

findings.title: failed list throws an uncaught RangeError on an out-of-range time in the state file
findings.command: Ledger with one failed entry; set its at to 9e15 in SQLite (src/ledger.ts:451 accepts any safe integer); bun --no-env-file src/index.ts failed list
findings.excerpt: RangeError: Invalid Date at describe (src/failed-cli.ts:27:24) at list (src/failed-cli.ts:62:27) at runCli (src/index.ts:671:20); exit 1 with a stack, documented codes are 0, 1 (bad usage) and 2 (state file unusable) with one line and no stack (docs/operation.md:48, :148).

notes: N1: Bun fetch uses HTTP_PROXY from the environment for webhook, Slack, Teams and api calls (postJson to a remote http URL with HTTP_PROXY set: 'posted', the local proxy got POST /hook). Undocumented; operator environment.

N2: the SMTP host and port of a database email channel are a connect target chosen by the api, internal addresses included. The report holds failed events without error codes. The secret case is security-notify-2026-11-07-1.
N3: bun audit: minimatch@10.2.6 moderate GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249, dev only (eslint via pulse-config), not in the image.
N4: Docker build stage runs apk add --no-cache git without a version pin; git is not in the final image.
N5: pulse-config is a dev dependency by SHA but not listed in docs/approved-packages.md.
N6: the ops listener has no authentication; the image binds 0.0.0.0:9100; /metrics shows channel ids (database ids too) and counters only.
N7: contract validators call one Proxy trap per call on a Proxy input and do not throw; a Proxy cannot come from JSON.parse.
N8: security-notify-2026-10-31-1, -2, -3, -4, -5, -7, -8 and -10 no longer reproduce on 0464b90.
